Subject: QBR prep: sprint-ready capacity check-in and OKR asks

Team —

We need a short, actionable update for leadership ahead of next week’s QBR. Topline asks (can you reply inline / with attachments by EOD Friday):

1) Demand & runway: updated 6-week GPU slot forecast (including burst assumptions for the retail holiday campaign). Call out margin of error and any single-point-of-failure.
2) Unit economics delta: current $/1000 tokens and projected $/1000 tokens if we onboard the suggested 4-bit quantized variant + prefix K/V cache for customer-facing routes.
3) Batching & cache outcomes: one-paragraph summary of the March experiments (latency tail, throughput, and P95 impact). Attach experiment PDFs.
4) Ask list for leadership: exactly what you need to move into Dedicated or increase reserved capacity (numbers + risk ladder).

I’ll synthesize into a 1-slide exec brief. Keep it short — bullets, clear asks, and anything that requires a leadership trade (credit, SLA exceptions, commit). Alyssa / Acme: sharing this so they see our assumptions relevant to the proposal.

Thanks —
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference
(attachment: sprint-ready-asklist-template.docx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: QBR prep: sprint-ready capacity check-in and OKR asks

Lauren —

Quick numbers, attached is a conservative forecast (gpu-util-forecast.xlsx). Highlights:
- Baseline weekly slots needed today: 1,200 (50% on-demand, 50% reserved).
- Six-week central case: +18% demand driven by retail pilot cadence (peak weeks add ~220 slots).
- Burst plan: we can provision 350 additional slots via marketplace burst with ~6h lead; cost per burst-slot ~1.9x reserved.
- Single SPOF: regional queuing on west-2 when P95 seq-length > 2k; mitigation: route some traffic to eu-west.

Unit economics (back-of-envelope):
- Current hosted $/1000 tokens: $0.68 (mixed M+L models, 70% short seqs).
- If we enable 4-bit quant + prefix K/V cache on 60% of traffic: projected $/1000 tokens down to ~$0.44 (material, but depends on model quality validation).

Notes: I pushed detailed numbers into the sheet (tab: six_week_forecast). If Marissa can confirm the cache hit assumptions we can lock the slide.

-Karthik
(attachment: gpu-util-forecast.xlsx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep: sprint-ready capacity check-in and OKR asks

Adding experiment context — TL;DR and attachments (batching-cache-results-0307.pdf).

Experiment summary (Mar 1–7):
- Workload: mixed chat + completion traffic mirroring Acme pilot routes (median seq ~160 tokens, 6% > 1500 tokens).
- Batching config A (aggressive batching): +38% throughput, median latency +12ms, P95 latency +60ms (not great for interactive routes).
- Batching config B (latency-aware batching): +18% throughput, median latency +6ms, P95 latency +18ms (safest win).
- K/V prefix cache at infra layer (cache hit tuned to 60%): reduced token compute by ~26% and reduced 95th latency by ~22% for cached flows.

Implications:
- For Acme-like interactive routes, prefer latency-aware batching + K/V cache; this gives most of the econ upside without blowing P95.
- If leadership wants max cost reduction, define routes eligible for aggressive batching (non-interactive background jobs). Need product signoff on route classification.

Attachment contains per-model breakouts and recommended thresholds. I also included a short rollout matrix (rollout-matrix.csv) for a staged switch to quantized variants across environments.

-Marissa
(attachment: batching-cache-results-0307.pdf; attachment: rollout-matrix.csv)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep: sprint-ready capacity check-in and OKR asks

Thanks — a few leadership-facing bullets to include in the slide deck: 

1) Recommendation: Approve staged capacity uplift of 300 reserved slots for the next 12 weeks (priority: west-2 then eu-west). Rationale: hedges forecasted retail peaks while keeping burst runway.
2) Trade: Financial ask is a one-time budget reallocation vs. a longer-term reserved commit. We should present two options: (A) temporary reserved top-up (12 weeks) vs. (B) 1yr moderate reserved commit (10% lower cost but 9-month minimum).
3) Quality guardrails for quantization: require model-level A/B evals against a 500-example synthetic prompt set (results must be within tolerance band before 30% traffic shift). Product & Applied ML to co-own.
4) Ops ask: priority routing policy to move long-seq traffic to non-latency-sensitive pools during peak. Requires 48–72h infra sprint to implement fallback rule.

I’ll draft the executive bullets — Lauren, do you want these in an appendix slide or on the main decision slide?

—Vivek

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>

- Marissa: produce the 2-slide experiment summary (one slide for latency-sensitive routes, one for background bulk routes) and attach A/B test criteria for quantization (due: Mon 3/20 EOD).
- Vivek: draft the two financial options and the fallback routing implementation estimate (dev hours + slack) for leadership (due: Mon 3/20 EOD).

I’ll assemble slides on Tue and circulate for final read by Wed morning. Thanks — short and focused.

Lauren
